info.title: Personal AI Coach — API contract review
info.description:
Review the proposed API inputs, outputs and errors before service implementation.

48 procedures are contract-only; 3 procedures are marked implemented.

This OpenAPI document projects the logical contracts into HTTP operations for review. The running application uses oRPC RPC; these are not published REST endpoints. Request execution is disabled.

Displayed JSON samples are generated from schemas; they are illustrations, not actual service responses or accepted business scenarios.

Result logs, habit logs and action logs each have a dedicated API group and model. Their wire collections use result_logs, habit_logs and action_logs. User billing fields derive from subscription and connected derives from oauth_consent.

Required, optional and nullable fields are generated from the canonical schemas. Cross-field checks and rules requiring stored state remain runtime/service obligations; read operation notes and the feature acceptance criteria.

## API and UI language

Wire names follow the current domain schema. Screen labels describe the same records from the user’s perspective; they do not introduce additional entities or enum values.

| API concept | Prototype UI label |
| --- | --- |
| Result logs | Updates; non-empty log comments also appear under Comments |
| Habit logs | Marked calendar days; Updates table with a Marked column |
| Action logs | Comments shows only logs with comments; status history remains in the API |
| Action status: open / in_progress / done | Open / In progress / Done; To do groups the first two |
| Cycle start_at / end_at; objective deadline_at; action due_at | Starts / Ends; Deadline; Due |
| Result metric_type; start_value / target_value; per | Type; Start / Target (Goal on chart); Times per Cadence |
| Session vendor: openai / claude | ChatGPT / Claude |
| Session briefing_notes / summary_notes / source_url | Briefing / Summary / Open the conversation |
| Session ended_at | In progress when null; Closed when set |
| Subscription past_due / incomplete | Payment failed / Awaiting payment |
| Subscription active with cancel_at_period_end | Cancels <date> with Access until; Cancellation scheduled when no period end is known |
| User name | Name; signup asks “What should we call you?” |
| Billing details plan / payment_method (null) | Plan and Price / Payment method (No subscription / No payment method) |

## Prototype alignment

Reconciled on 2 Oct 2026 (CB-049 Reconcile API and prototype language differences); the prototype was revised in its design source and these now agree:

- **Profile name:** Settings has one Name field and signup asks “What should we call you?”, matching the single chosen `name`.

- **Entity wording:** prototype authoring notes and fixture identifiers say ResultLog and HabitLog; visible Updates and Marked remain UI copy.

- **Payment failure:** paid access is active-only; past-due, canceled and incomplete keep reads and block coaching writes and session starts, with no grace-period promise.

- **Objective deadline:** an update accepts an omitted field or a date; null is rejected on API and MCP alike. Creation without a deadline stays valid and the returned value stays nullable.

- **Billing details:** Settings reads Plan, Price and Payment method from `billing.get_billing_details`, which loads independently and fails with a retryable error without blocking local status.

- **Scheduled cancellation:** the prototype derives it from active status, cancel-at-period-end and the period end; there is no fifth status.

**Open:** `user.update` is declared `entitled-write`, while the revised prototype keeps Name, Time zone and About me editable for a lapsed plan. Awaiting a decision on which side changes.

**Access:** authenticated session; policy `account-management`. Identity is resolved server-side.

Web-only read of the selected subscription plan, price and effective payment method for Settings. The account and customer resolve server-side. This is the only read that may contact the billing provider; user.get and coaching reads never do. No subscription returns null plan and payment method without a provider call. A transient provider failure returns SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE with error_code billing_details_unavailable; unsupported or unresolvable billing data also fails explicitly and is never reported as no subscription. Display only: it never grants entitlement, and a portal return re-reads it. Not an MCP tool.
